source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ אֵלִיָּ֛הוּ וֶאֱלִישָׁ֖ע מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when took up Yahweh Elijah in the whirlwind [to] the heavens, and went Elijah and Elisha from the Gilgal.

en.L: And it came about, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was taking Elijah up in the whirlwind [to] the heavens, that Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was about to take Elijah up to heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were setting out from Gilgal.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was about to take Elijah up into heaven in a whirlwind. At that time Elijah and Elisha were leaving the town of Gilgal.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} iba a subir a Elías en el torbellino [a] los cielos, Elías y Eliseo salieron de Gilgal.
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba a punto de llevarse a Elías al cielo en un torbellino, Elías y Eliseo salían de Gilgal.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba a punto de llevarse a Elías al cielo en un torbellino. En ese tiempo Elías y Eliseo salían del pueblo de Gilgal.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} enleva Élie dans le tourbillon [vers] les cieux, qu’Élie et Élisée partirent de Guilgal.
fr.B: Au moment où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} allait enlever Élie au ciel dans un tourbillon, Élie et Élisée partaient de Guilgal.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} allait bientôt emmener Élie au ciel dans un tourbillon. À ce moment-là, Élie et Élisée quittaient la ville de Guilgal.

sw.L: Ikawa, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipokuwa akimpandisha Eliya katika kisulisuli [kwenda] mbinguni, Eliya na Elisha wakaondoka Gilgali.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipokuwa karibu kumpandisha Eliya mbinguni kwa kisulisuli, Eliya na Elisha walikuwa wakiondoka Gilgali.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa karibu kumchukua Eliya mbinguni katika upepo mkali wa kisulisuli. Wakati huo Eliya na Elisha walikuwa wakiondoka katika mji wa Gilgali.

vi.L: Khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cất Ê-li lên trời trong cơn gió lốc, thì Ê-li và Ê-li-sê đi khỏi Ghinh-ganh.
vi.B: Khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sắp cất Ê-li lên trời bằng một cơn gió lốc, Ê-li và Ê-li-sê đang rời Ghinh-ganh.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sắp đem Ê-li lên trời trong một cơn gió lốc. Lúc ấy Ê-li và Ê-li-sê đang rời thị trấn Ghinh-ganh.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 엘리야를 회오리바람으로 하늘로 데려 올리실 때에, 엘리야와 엘리사가 길갈에서 떠났다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 엘리야를 회오리바람에 실어 하늘로 데려가려고 하실 때에, 엘리야와 엘리사는 길갈을 떠나고 있었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 엘리야를 회오리바람에 실어 하늘로 데려가려고 하셨다. 그때 엘리야와 엘리사는 길갈 마을을 떠나고 있었다.

decisions.choice: when Yahweh was taking Elijah up: the opening tells the reader what is about to happen
decisions.reason: The first words name the end of the story before it starts: the day Yahweh took Elijah up. Elijah himself (verses 9-10), Elisha and the company of prophets (verses 3, 5) all know it is coming. The verb form says when the journey happened, not that Elijah was already rising.

decisions.choice: the whirlwind: a violent storm wind sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word names a storm or gale, the kind of wind in which Yahweh appears and speaks (Job 38:1; Ezekiel 1:4). It is called "the" whirlwind because the story goes on to tell of it (verse 11). Elijah is carried up by the wind; the chariot of fire separates the two men (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Gilgal: probably a town in the hill country, not the camp by the Jordan
decisions.reason: From this Gilgal the two men "went down" to Bethel (verse 2), so it lay higher than Bethel, in the hills. The Gilgal where Israel camped after crossing the Jordan (Joshua 4:19) lay low near Jericho, which they reach only later (verse 4). The exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: were setting out / were leaving
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the journey was starting, since verse 1 sets the scene for the walk that follows.

decisions.choice: the town of Gilgal
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so the reader knows this is a place name.

decisions.choice: "le tourbillon" (L); "un tourbillon" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Tourbillon" says the violent whirling wind of the Hebrew; the article follows the Hebrew at L and French usage at B and R.

decisions.choice: "kisulisuli" (whirlwind)
decisions.reason: "Kisulisuli" is a wind that spins and rises, the picture of the Hebrew word for a violent storm wind; Readable adds "upepo mkali wa" so the word is clear.

decisions.choice: "cơn gió lốc"
decisions.reason: The word is a violent storm wind sent by God (m2); "gió lốc" (whirlwind) keeps the picture of a wind that lifts.

decisions.choice: "회오리바람" for the whirlwind at every level
decisions.reason: "회오리바람" is the common word for a whirling storm wind and fits the picture of Elijah being carried up (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֜ע שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי עַד־בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּרְד֖וּ בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Elijah to Elisha, Stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me as far as Bethel; and said Elisha, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and they went down [to] Bethel.

en.L: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me as far as Bethel." And Elisha said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And they went down [to] Bethel.
en.B: Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me on to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." Then they went down together to Bethel.
en.R: Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went down to Bethel.

es.L: Y Elías dijo a Eliseo: «Quédate aquí, te ruego, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado hasta Betel». Y Eliseo dijo: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y vive tu alma, que no te dejaré». Y descendieron [a] Betel.
es.B: Elías le dijo a Eliseo: «Por favor, quédate aquí, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me envía a Betel». Pero Eliseo respondió: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Y bajaron juntos a Betel.
es.R: Elías le dijo a Eliseo: «Por favor, quédate aquí. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado a Betel». Pero Eliseo le contestó: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Así que los dos bajaron a Betel.

fr.L: Et Élie dit à Élisée : « Reste ici, je te prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie jusqu’à Béthel. » Et Élisée dit : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et [que] ton âme est vivante, je ne te quitterai pas. » Et ils descendirent [à] Béthel.
fr.B: Élie dit à Élisée : « Reste ici, je t’en prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie jusqu’à Béthel. » Mais Élisée répondit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Et ils descendirent ensemble à Béthel.
fr.R: Élie a dit à Élisée : « Reste ici, s’il te plaît. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie à Béthel. » Mais Élisée a répondu : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Alors ils sont descendus tous les deux à Béthel.

sw.L: Eliya akamwambia Elisha, "Tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma mpaka Betheli." Elisha akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama roho yako iishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wakashuka [mpaka] Betheli.
sw.B: Eliya akamwambia Elisha, "Tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma niende Betheli." Lakini Elisha akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wakashuka pamoja mpaka Betheli.
sw.R: Eliya akamwambia Elisha, "Tafadhali kaa hapa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma Betheli." Lakini Elisha akajibu, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wote wawili wakashuka mpaka Betheli.

vi.L: Ê-li nói với Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai ta đến tận Bê-tên." Ê-li-sê nói: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như linh hồn thầy hằng sống, con sẽ không lìa thầy." Vậy họ đi xuống Bê-tên.
vi.B: Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đi đến Bê-tên." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Thế là hai thầy trò cùng đi xuống Bê-tên.
vi.R: Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đi Bê-tên." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Vậy hai thầy trò cùng đi xuống Bê-tên.

ko.L: 그리고 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "너는 제발 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 벧엘까지 보내셨다." 그러자 엘리사가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님의 영혼이 살아 있음을 [두고 맹세하는데], 제가 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그리고 그들이 벧엘로 내려갔다.
ko.B: 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "너는 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 벧엘로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 그들은 함께 벧엘로 내려갔다.
ko.R: 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "너는 여기 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 벧엘로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세합니다. 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 두 사람은 벧엘로 내려갔다.

decisions.choice: stay here, please: a request, perhaps also a test
decisions.reason: Elijah asks three times (verses 2, 4, 6) and Elisha refuses three times. The story does not say why Elijah asks: to spare Elisha, to go alone, or to see whether Elisha will hold on to him. Elisha's refusals show his loyalty to the end (compare Ruth 1:15-18).

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives: a double oath
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath; Elisha adds the life of Elijah himself, as Jonathan and Abigail did with David (1 Samuel 20:3; 25:26). "Your soul" means simply "you" in person.

decisions.choice: if I leave you: means "I will not leave you"
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if I do this" leaves an unspoken curse on the speaker, so it means "I will certainly not do this" (1 Kings 17:1).

decisions.choice: Bethel: an old place of worship, and a center of the calf worship of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Bethel was where Jacob met God (Genesis 28:19). Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves there (1 Kings 12:28-29), and yet a company of prophets loyal to Yahweh lived there (verse 3).

decisions.choice: [as] your soul lives / as surely as you live
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 1 Samuel 20:3 and 25:26. Literal keeps "your soul"; Balanced and Readable say "you", which is what it means (m2). Literal says "I will not leave you" for the oath form (m3).

decisions.choice: Vive el SEÑOR y vive tu alma (Literal); tan cierto como que el SEÑOR vive y tan cierto como que tú vives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The oath keeps the wording of the Spanish of Samuel; Literal keeps "tu alma", Balanced and Readable say "tú", which is what it means.

decisions.choice: "que ton âme est vivante" (L); "que tu es vivant" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath formula of the French Samuel drafts, "Aussi vrai que le SEIGNEUR est vivant"; Literal keeps the Hebrew "your soul", Balanced and Readable say "you" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "kama roho yako iishivyo" (Literal); "kama wewe uishivyo" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The double oath follows the Samuel wording "Kama BWANA aishivyo". Literal keeps "your soul"; Balanced and Readable say "you", which is what it means.

decisions.choice: Elijah says "ta" and "con" to Elisha; Elisha says "thầy" and "con"
decisions.reason: Elisha is Elijah's attendant and disciple (1 Kings 19:21), so the pair speak as master and pupil; verse 12 adds "cha" where the Hebrew says "my father".

decisions.choice: "Thật như CHÚA hằng sống và như linh hồn thầy hằng sống" (L); "... và như thầy đang sống" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's oath formula; "your soul" is the person himself, so Balanced and Readable say "thầy".

decisions.choice: Elijah speaks to Elisha in the plain style (해라체); Elisha answers his master in 합쇼체, calling him "선생님"
decisions.reason: A prophet and the disciple who serves him (1 Kings 19:21) speak as teacher and pupil; "선생님" is the ordinary respectful address to a teacher.

decisions.choice: The double oath as "...살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데"; Literal keeps "영혼" for "soul"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for "As the LORD lives"; Balanced and Readable say "as you live", as the English does.

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בֵּֽית־אֵל֮ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הֲיָדַ֕עְתָּ כִּ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם יְהוָ֛ה לֹקֵ֥חַ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ מֵעַ֣ל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־אֲנִ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי הֶחֱשֽׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came out [the] sons of the prophets who [were at] Bethel to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today Yahweh [is] taking your master from over your head? And he said, Also I know; be silent.

en.L: And the sons of the prophets who [were at] Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know [it]; be silent."
en.B: The company of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master from you today?" He said, "Yes, I know. Say no more."
en.R: A group of prophets lived at Bethel. They came out to meet Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master away from you today?" "Yes, I know," Elisha said. "Do not talk about it."

es.L: Y los hijos de los profetas que [estaban en] Betel salieron a Eliseo y le dijeron: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} va a quitar a tu señor de sobre tu cabeza?». Y él dijo: «También yo [lo] sé; {{plural_you:callen|callad}}».
es.B: Los discípulos de los profetas que había en Betel salieron al encuentro de Eliseo y le preguntaron: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se va a llevar a tu maestro?». Él respondió: «Sí, ya lo sé. No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} más».
es.R: En Betel vivía un grupo de profetas. Salieron al encuentro de Eliseo y le preguntaron: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se va a llevar a tu maestro?». «Sí, ya lo sé», dijo Eliseo. «No {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} de eso».

fr.L: Et les fils des prophètes qui [étaient à] Béthel sortirent vers Élisée et lui dirent : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} enlève ton maître de dessus ta tête ? » Et il dit : « Moi aussi, je [le] sais ; taisez-vous. »
fr.B: Les disciples des prophètes qui étaient à Béthel sortirent à la rencontre d’Élisée et lui demandèrent : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va t’enlever ton maître ? » Il répondit : « Oui, je le sais. N’en dites pas plus. »
fr.R: Un groupe de prophètes vivait à Béthel. Ils sont sortis à la rencontre d’Élisée et lui ont demandé : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va t’enlever ton maître ? » Élisée a répondu : « Oui, je le sais. N’en parlez pas. »

sw.L: Wana wa manabii waliokuwa Betheli wakatoka kwa Elisha, wakamwambia, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anamchukua bwana wako kutoka juu ya kichwa chako?" Akasema, "Mimi nami najua; nyamazeni."
sw.B: Kundi la manabii waliokuwa Betheli lilimjia Elisha, likamwuliza, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamchukua bwana wako kutoka kwako?" Akasema, "Ndiyo, najua. Msiseme zaidi."
sw.R: Kundi la manabii lilikaa Betheli. Walitoka kwenda kumlaki Elisha, wakamwuliza, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamchukua bwana wako akuache?" Elisha akasema, "Ndiyo, najua. Msiseme habari hiyo."

vi.L: Các con trai của các nhà tiên tri ở Bê-tên đi ra gặp Ê-li-sê và nói với ông: "Ông có biết rằng hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ cất thầy của ông khỏi đầu ông không?" Ông nói: "Tôi cũng biết; hãy im lặng."
vi.B: Đoàn tiên tri ở Bê-tên đi ra gặp Ê-li-sê và hỏi: "Ông có biết hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ cất thầy của ông đi khỏi ông không?" Ông đáp: "Vâng, tôi biết. Đừng nói nữa."
vi.R: Ở Bê-tên có một đoàn tiên tri. Họ đi ra gặp Ê-li-sê và hỏi: "Ông có biết hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem thầy của ông đi khỏi ông không?" Ê-li-sê đáp: "Vâng, tôi biết. Đừng nói đến chuyện ấy."

ko.L: 그리고 벧엘에 있는 예언자의 아들들이 엘리사에게 나와서 그에게 말했다. "오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신의 주인을 당신의 머리 위에서 데려가시려는 것을 당신은 아시오?" 그러자 그가 말했다. "나도 알고 있소. 잠잠하시오."
ko.B: 벧엘에 있는 예언자 무리가 엘리사에게 나와서 물었다. "오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신의 스승을 당신에게서 데려가시려는 것을 아시오?" 엘리사가 말했다. "나도 알고 있소. 더 말하지 마시오."
ko.R: 벧엘에는 예언자 무리가 살고 있었다. 그들이 엘리사를 맞으러 나와서 물었다. "오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신의 스승을 당신에게서 데려가실 것을 아시오?" 엘리사가 말했다. "나도 알고 있소. 그 이야기는 하지 마시오."

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: members of a company of prophets
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means members of a group, not children. These were bands of prophets who lived and worked together, apparently under a leader they called "father" (verse 12; 6:1-2; 1 Kings 20:35). Elijah seems to have led them, and Elisha takes his place (verse 15).

decisions.choice: from over your head: away from you, as the one who stands over you
decisions.reason: Elijah is Elisha's master, the one above him. To take him "from over your head" is to remove him from his place as Elisha's leader. It may also hint at Elijah being taken up.

decisions.choice: I also know; be silent: Elisha already knows and does not want it spoken of
decisions.reason: Elisha knows as well as they do. His command to be quiet shows grief or that the matter is not for talk; he says no more and stays with his master.

decisions.choice: company of prophets
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of the prophets"; Balanced says "company of prophets" and Readable "group of prophets", as m1 explains.

decisions.choice: Say no more / Do not talk about it
decisions.reason: The command "be silent" means "do not speak of it", not that they had been shouting.

decisions.choice: los hijos de los profetas (Literal); los discípulos de los profetas (Balanced); el grupo de profetas (Readable)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording at each level: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, Balanced and Readable say what it means, members of a company of prophets (m1).

decisions.choice: tu maestro
decisions.reason: Elijah is Elisha's master as teacher and leader of a prophet's disciple, so Balanced and Readable say "maestro"; Literal keeps "tu señor".

decisions.choice: "les fils des prophètes" (L); "les disciples des prophètes" (B); "un groupe de prophètes" (R)
alternatives: "les fils des prophètes" at every level
decisions.reason: As the Kings terms note, for the whole block.

decisions.choice: "wana wa manabii" (Literal); "kundi la manabii" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the terms note for Kings: Literal keeps "sons of the prophets", Balanced and Readable say what they were, a company of prophets.

decisions.choice: "các con trai của các nhà tiên tri" (L); "đoàn tiên tri" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for the sons of the prophets, a company of prophets (m1).

decisions.choice: the prophets call Elisha "ông" and themselves "chúng tôi"; he says "tôi" and "các anh"
decisions.reason: Members of the same company speak politely; Elisha is not yet their leader (verse 15).

decisions.choice: "예언자의 아들들" (L), "예언자 무리" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note.

decisions.choice: Elisha and the prophets speak to each other in 하오체, as men of one company; "your master" is "당신의 주인" (L), "당신의 스승" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Before Elijah is taken, Elisha is one of the prophets' peers; 하오체 is the respectful address between grown men. "스승" says what kind of master Elijah was to Elisha.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע׀שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי יְרִיח֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Elijah, Elisha, stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me [to] Jericho; and he said, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and they came [to] Jericho.

en.L: And Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me [to] Jericho." And he said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And they came [to] Jericho.
en.B: Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
en.R: Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Jericho." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they went on to Jericho.

es.L: Y Elías le dijo: «Eliseo, quédate aquí, te ruego, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado [a] Jericó». Y él dijo: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y vive tu alma, que no te dejaré». Y llegaron [a] Jericó.
es.B: Entonces Elías le dijo: «Eliseo, por favor, quédate aquí, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me envía a Jericó». Pero él respondió: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Así llegaron a Jericó.
es.R: Entonces Elías le dijo: «Eliseo, por favor, quédate aquí. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado a Jericó». Pero Eliseo le contestó: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Así que siguieron hasta Jericó.

fr.L: Et Élie lui dit : « Élisée, reste ici, je te prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie [à] Jéricho. » Et il dit : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et [que] ton âme est vivante, je ne te quitterai pas. » Et ils arrivèrent [à] Jéricho.
fr.B: Puis Élie lui dit : « Élisée, reste ici, je t’en prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie à Jéricho. » Mais il répondit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Ils arrivèrent donc à Jéricho.
fr.R: Puis Élie lui a dit : « Élisée, reste ici, s’il te plaît. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie à Jéricho. » Mais Élisée a répondu : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Alors ils ont continué jusqu’à Jéricho.

sw.L: Eliya akamwambia, "Elisha, tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma [mpaka] Yeriko." Akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama roho yako iishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wakafika [mpaka] Yeriko.
sw.B: Kisha Eliya akamwambia, "Elisha, tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma niende Yeriko." Lakini akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wakafika Yeriko.
sw.R: Kisha Eliya akamwambia, "Elisha, tafadhali kaa hapa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma Yeriko." Lakini Elisha akajibu, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wakaendelea mpaka Yeriko.

vi.L: Ê-li nói với Ê-li-sê: "Ê-li-sê, con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai ta đến Giê-ri-cô." Ê-li-sê nói: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như linh hồn thầy hằng sống, con sẽ không lìa thầy." Vậy họ đến Giê-ri-cô.
vi.B: Rồi Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Ê-li-sê, con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đi đến Giê-ri-cô." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Vậy họ đến Giê-ri-cô.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Ê-li-sê, con hãy ở lại đây. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đi Giê-ri-cô." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Vậy họ đi tiếp đến Giê-ri-cô.

ko.L: 그리고 엘리야가 그에게 말했다. "엘리사야, 너는 제발 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 여리고로 보내셨다." 그러자 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님의 영혼이 살아 있음을 [두고 맹세하는데], 제가 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그리고 그들이 여리고로 갔다.
ko.B: 엘리야가 또 그에게 말했다. "엘리사야, 너는 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 여리고로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 그들은 여리고로 갔다.
ko.R: 엘리야가 또 그에게 말했다. "엘리사야, 너는 여기 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 여리고로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세합니다. 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 두 사람은 여리고로 갔다.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives, if I leave you: a firm oath that he will not leave
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Jericho: the city near the Jordan, rebuilt in Ahab's time
decisions.reason: Joshua had laid a curse on anyone who rebuilt Jericho (Joshua 6:26), and it fell on Hiel of Bethel in Ahab's days (1 Kings 16:34). Now prophets of Yahweh live there (verse 5), and Elisha will heal its water (verses 19-22).

records.literal_gloss: And drew near [the] sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today Yahweh [is] taking your master from over your head? And he said, Also I know; be silent.

en.L: And the sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know [it]; be silent."
en.B: The company of prophets who were at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master from you today?" He answered, "Yes, I know. Say no more."
en.R: The group of prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master away from you today?" "Yes, I know," he answered. "Do not talk about it."

es.L: Y los hijos de los profetas que [estaban] en Jericó se acercaron a Eliseo y le dijeron: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} va a quitar a tu señor de sobre tu cabeza?». Y él dijo: «También yo [lo] sé; {{plural_you:callen|callad}}».
es.B: Los discípulos de los profetas que estaban en Jericó se acercaron a Eliseo y le dijeron: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se va a llevar a tu maestro?». Él respondió: «Sí, ya lo sé. No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} más».
es.R: El grupo de profetas de Jericó se acercó a Eliseo y le preguntó: «¿Sabes que hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se va a llevar a tu maestro?». «Sí, ya lo sé», respondió él. «No {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} de eso».

fr.L: Et les fils des prophètes qui [étaient] à Jéricho s’approchèrent d’Élisée et lui dirent : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} enlève ton maître de dessus ta tête ? » Et il dit : « Moi aussi, je [le] sais ; taisez-vous. »
fr.B: Les disciples des prophètes qui étaient à Jéricho s’approchèrent d’Élisée et lui dirent : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va t’enlever ton maître ? » Il répondit : « Oui, je le sais. N’en dites pas plus. »
fr.R: Le groupe de prophètes de Jéricho s’est approché d’Élisée et lui a demandé : « Sais-tu qu’aujourd’hui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va t’enlever ton maître ? » Élisée a répondu : « Oui, je le sais. N’en parlez pas. »

sw.L: Wana wa manabii waliokuwa huko Yeriko wakamkaribia Elisha, wakamwambia, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anamchukua bwana wako kutoka juu ya kichwa chako?" Akasema, "Mimi nami najua; nyamazeni."
sw.B: Kundi la manabii waliokuwa huko Yeriko lilimkaribia Elisha, likamwambia, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamchukua bwana wako kutoka kwako?" Akajibu, "Ndiyo, najua. Msiseme zaidi."
sw.R: Kundi la manabii la Yeriko likamjia Elisha, wakamwuliza, "Je, unajua kwamba leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamchukua bwana wako akuache?" Akajibu, "Ndiyo, najua. Msiseme habari hiyo."

decisions.reason: The prophets at Jericho repeat the words of those at Bethel (verse 3), and Elisha answers the same way. The repetition slows the story as the moment comes near.

decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Elijah, Stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me to the Jordan; and he said, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and went the two of them.

en.L: And Elijah said to him, "Stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan." And he said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And the two of them went on.
en.B: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." And the two of them walked on.
en.R: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan River." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them kept walking together.

es.L: Y Elías le dijo: «Quédate aquí, te ruego, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado al Jordán». Y él dijo: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y vive tu alma, que no te dejaré». Y siguieron los dos.
es.B: Entonces Elías le dijo: «Por favor, quédate aquí, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me envía al Jordán». Pero él respondió: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Y los dos siguieron caminando.
es.R: Entonces Elías le dijo: «Por favor, quédate aquí. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha enviado al río Jordán». Pero Eliseo le contestó: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive y tan cierto como que tú vives, no te dejaré». Así que los dos siguieron caminando juntos.

fr.L: Et Élie lui dit : « Reste ici, je te prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie au Jourdain. » Et il dit : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et [que] ton âme est vivante, je ne te quitterai pas. » Et ils s’en allèrent tous les deux.
fr.B: Puis Élie lui dit : « Reste ici, je t’en prie, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie au Jourdain. » Mais il répondit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Et tous deux poursuivirent leur chemin.
fr.R: Puis Élie lui a dit : « Reste ici, s’il te plaît. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’envoie au fleuve du Jourdain. » Mais Élisée a répondu : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant et que tu es vivant, je ne te quitterai pas. » Alors ils ont continué à marcher ensemble.

sw.L: Eliya akamwambia, "Tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma mpaka Yordani." Akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama roho yako iishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wote wawili wakaendelea.
sw.B: Kisha Eliya akamwambia, "Tafadhali kaa hapa, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma niende Yordani." Lakini akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wote wawili wakaendelea kutembea.
sw.R: Kisha Eliya akamwambia, "Tafadhali kaa hapa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenituma mpaka mto Yordani." Lakini Elisha akajibu, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, na kama wewe uishivyo, sitakuacha." Basi wote wawili wakaendelea kutembea pamoja.

vi.L: Ê-li nói với Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã sai ta đến sông Giô-đanh." Ê-li-sê nói: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như linh hồn thầy hằng sống, con sẽ không lìa thầy." Và cả hai người cùng đi.
vi.B: Rồi Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đi đến sông Giô-đanh." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Vậy hai thầy trò cùng đi tiếp.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Con hãy ở lại đây. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai ta đến sông Giô-đanh." Nhưng Ê-li-sê thưa: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống và như thầy đang sống, con sẽ không rời thầy đâu." Vậy hai thầy trò tiếp tục cùng đi.

ko.L: 그리고 엘리야가 그에게 말했다. "너는 제발 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 요단으로 보내셨다." 그러자 그가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님의 영혼이 살아 있음을 [두고 맹세하는데], 제가 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그리고 그 두 사람이 계속 갔다.
ko.B: 엘리야가 또 그에게 말했다. "너는 여기 머물러 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 요단강으로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 두 사람은 계속 걸어갔다.
ko.R: 엘리야가 또 그에게 말했다. "너는 여기 있어라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 요단강으로 보내셨다." 그러나 엘리사가 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심과 선생님께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세합니다. 저는 선생님을 떠나지 않겠습니다." 그래서 두 사람은 함께 계속 걸어갔다.

decisions.choice: the oath a third time
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. The third refusal shows that Elisha will not be turned back.

decisions.choice: the Jordan: the river east of Jericho
decisions.reason: Elijah came from Gilead, east of the Jordan (1 Kings 17:1). His journey leads him back across the river, toward the region where Moses was taken from Israel (Deuteronomy 34:1-6).

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" so the reader knows what the Jordan is.

source.text: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֨ים אִ֜ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֤י הַנְּבִיאִים֙ הָֽלְכ֔וּ וַיַּעַמְד֥וּ מִנֶּ֖גֶד מֵרָח֑וֹק וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם עָמְד֥וּ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And fifty men from [the] sons of the prophets went and stood opposite at a distance; and the two of them stood by the Jordan.

en.L: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite [them] at a distance, and the two of them stood by the Jordan.
en.B: Fifty men of the company of prophets went along and stood some distance away, facing them, while the two of them stood beside the Jordan.
en.R: Fifty men from the group of prophets also went. They stood a long way off and watched, while Elijah and Elisha stood beside the Jordan.

es.L: Y cincuenta hombres de los hijos de los profetas fueron y se pararon enfrente, a lo lejos; y los dos se pararon junto al Jordán.
es.B: Cincuenta hombres de los discípulos de los profetas fueron también y se quedaron a cierta distancia, frente a ellos, mientras los dos se detenían junto al Jordán.
es.R: Cincuenta hombres del grupo de profetas también fueron. Se quedaron lejos y miraban, mientras Elías y Eliseo se detenían a la orilla del Jordán.

fr.L: Et cinquante hommes d’entre les fils des prophètes allèrent et se tinrent en face, à distance ; et tous deux se tinrent au bord du Jourdain.
fr.B: Cinquante hommes d’entre les disciples des prophètes les suivirent et s’arrêtèrent à quelque distance, face à eux, tandis que tous deux se tenaient au bord du Jourdain.
fr.R: Cinquante hommes du groupe de prophètes y sont allés aussi. Ils sont restés loin et ils regardaient, pendant qu’Élie et Élisée se tenaient au bord du Jourdain.

sw.L: Watu hamsini wa wana wa manabii wakaenda, wakasimama kuwaelekea kwa mbali; nao wote wawili wakasimama kando ya Yordani.
sw.B: Watu hamsini wa kundi la manabii walikwenda pia, wakasimama mbali kidogo wakiwatazama, huku wale wawili wakisimama kando ya Yordani.
sw.R: Watu hamsini wa kundi la manabii nao walikwenda. Wakasimama mbali, wakatazama, huku Eliya na Elisha wakisimama kando ya mto Yordani.

vi.L: Năm mươi người trong các con trai của các nhà tiên tri đi theo và đứng đối diện ở đằng xa, còn hai người kia đứng bên sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Năm mươi người trong đoàn tiên tri cũng đi theo và đứng nhìn từ xa, còn hai thầy trò thì đứng bên bờ sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Năm mươi người trong đoàn tiên tri cũng đi theo. Họ đứng thật xa mà nhìn, còn Ê-li và Ê-li-sê đứng bên bờ sông Giô-đanh.

ko.L: 그리고 예언자의 아들들 가운데 오십 명이 가서 멀리 맞은편에 섰고, 그 두 사람은 요단 가에 섰다.
ko.B: 예언자 무리 가운데 오십 명이 따라가서 멀리 떨어져 그들을 마주 보고 섰고, 그 두 사람은 요단강 가에 섰다.
ko.R: 예언자 무리 가운데 오십 명도 따라갔다. 그들은 멀리 떨어져 서서 지켜보았고, 엘리야와 엘리사는 요단강 가에 섰다.

decisions.choice: stood opposite at a distance: they watched from far off
decisions.reason: The prophets keep their distance but stand where they can see. They are witnesses of what happens at the river (verse 15).

decisions.choice: watched; Elijah and Elisha
decisions.reason: Readable says that the men watched, which standing "opposite" implies, and names the two men for clarity.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶת־אַדַּרְתּ֤וֹ וַיִּגְלֹם֙ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם וַיֵּחָצ֖וּ הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֑נָּה וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בֶּחָרָבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Elijah his cloak and rolled [it] up and struck the waters, and they were divided here and here, and crossed the two of them on dry ground.

en.L: And Elijah took his cloak and rolled [it] up and struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that way, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
en.B: Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water. The water divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
en.R: Then Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up and hit the water with it. The water split apart, part to one side and part to the other. And the two of them walked across on dry ground.

es.L: Y tomó Elías su manto, y [lo] enrolló y golpeó las aguas, y se dividieron a un lado y a otro, y pasaron los dos en seco.
es.B: Entonces Elías tomó su manto, lo enrolló y golpeó el agua. El agua se dividió a un lado y a otro, y los dos cruzaron por tierra seca.
es.R: Entonces Elías se quitó el manto, lo enrolló y golpeó el agua con él. El agua se abrió, una parte hacia un lado y otra hacia el otro, y los dos cruzaron caminando por tierra seca.

fr.L: Et Élie prit son manteau, le roula et frappa les eaux ; et elles se divisèrent de-ci et de-là, et ils passèrent tous les deux à pied sec.
fr.B: Alors Élie prit son manteau, le roula et frappa l’eau. L’eau se partagea d’un côté et de l’autre, et tous deux traversèrent à pied sec.
fr.R: Alors Élie a enlevé son manteau, il l’a roulé et il a frappé l’eau avec. L’eau s’est séparée : une partie d’un côté, une partie de l’autre. Et tous les deux ont traversé à pied sec.

sw.L: Eliya akalitwaa vazi lake, akalikunja, akayapiga maji, nayo yakagawanyika huku na huku, nao wote wawili wakavuka pakavu.
sw.B: Kisha Eliya akalichukua vazi lake, akalikunja, akayapiga maji. Maji yakagawanyika upande huu na upande huu, nao wote wawili wakavuka pakavu.
sw.R: Kisha Eliya akavua vazi lake, akalikunja, akayapiga maji kwa vazi hilo. Maji yakagawanyika, sehemu moja upande mmoja na sehemu nyingine upande mwingine. Nao wote wawili wakavuka wakitembea pakavu.

vi.L: Ê-li lấy áo choàng của mình, cuộn lại và đập xuống nước; nước rẽ ra bên này và bên kia, và cả hai người đi qua trên đất khô.
vi.B: Ê-li lấy áo choàng của mình, cuộn lại rồi đập xuống nước. Nước rẽ ra hai bên, và hai thầy trò đi qua trên đất khô.
vi.R: Ê-li cởi áo choàng ra, cuộn lại và đập xuống mặt nước. Nước tách ra, một phần sang bên này, một phần sang bên kia. Hai thầy trò đi bộ qua sông trên đất khô.

ko.L: 그리고 엘리야가 자기 겉옷을 가져다가 말아서 물을 쳤다. 그러자 물이 이쪽과 저쪽으로 갈라졌고, 그 두 사람이 마른 땅으로 건너갔다.
ko.B: 엘리야가 자기 겉옷을 벗어 말아서 물을 쳤다. 그러자 물이 이쪽저쪽으로 갈라졌고, 두 사람은 마른 땅을 밟고 건너갔다.
ko.R: 엘리야가 겉옷을 벗어서 둘둘 말아 그것으로 물을 쳤다. 그러자 물이 이쪽과 저쪽으로 갈라졌다. 두 사람은 마른 땅을 밟고 걸어서 건너갔다.

decisions.choice: the waters divided and they crossed on dry ground: as at the sea and at the Jordan before
decisions.reason: The words recall Moses stretching out his staff over the sea so that Israel crossed on dry ground (Exodus 14:16, 21-22), and the Jordan stopping for Israel under Joshua (Joshua 3:13-17), where the same word for dry ground is used. Elijah's cloak does what Moses' staff did, and the Jordan crossing is made again, this time in the other direction.

decisions.choice: his cloak: the prophet's outer garment, the mark of his office
decisions.reason: Elijah threw this cloak over Elisha when he called him (1 Kings 19:19), and wrapped his face in it on Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:13). Elisha will take it up (verse 13).

decisions.choice: rolled it up: folded or wrapped it together
decisions.reason: This verb is found only here. It seems to mean that Elijah rolled the cloak into a bundle, like a rod, to strike the water.

decisions.choice: this way and that way / to one side and the other
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "hither and hither"; the water stood on both sides of the path.

decisions.choice: "áo choàng"
decisions.reason: The prophet's outer garment (m2); "áo choàng" names a cloak without making it a raincoat.

decisions.choice: "겉옷" for Elijah's cloak at every level
decisions.reason: "겉옷" is the plain word for an outer garment; "망토" sounds foreign and modern. The same word is used when the cloak falls to Elisha (verses 13-14).

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְעָבְרָ֗ם וְאֵ֨לִיָּ֜הוּ אָמַ֤ר אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֙ שְׁאַל֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֶלָּקַ֣ח מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וִֽיהִי־נָ֛א פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֥יִם בְּרוּחֲךָ֖ אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as they crossed, and Elijah said to Elisha, Ask what I may do for you before I am taken from with you; and said Elisha, And let be please a mouth of two in your spirit to me.

en.L: And it came about, as they crossed, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "Please let there be a double portion of your spirit for me."
en.B: When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Before I am taken from you, tell me what I can do for you." Elisha answered, "Please let me receive a double portion of your spirit."
en.R: After they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "I am about to be taken away from you. Before that happens, what can I do for you? Ask me." Elisha answered, "Please give me a double share of your spirit, the share that goes to a firstborn son."

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando pasaron, Elías dijo a Eliseo: «Pide qué haré por ti antes de que sea quitado de contigo». Y Eliseo dijo: «Te ruego que haya para mí una doble porción de tu espíritu».
es.B: Cuando ya habían cruzado, Elías le dijo a Eliseo: «Antes de que me lleven de tu lado, dime qué puedo hacer por ti». Eliseo respondió: «Te ruego que me toque una doble porción de tu espíritu».
es.R: Después de cruzar, Elías le dijo a Eliseo: «Estoy a punto de ser llevado lejos de ti. Antes de que eso pase, ¿qué puedo hacer por ti? Pídemelo». Eliseo respondió: «Por favor, dame una doble porción de tu espíritu, la parte que le toca al hijo mayor».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand ils eurent passé, qu’Élie dit à Élisée : « Demande ce que je ferai pour toi avant que je sois enlevé d’avec toi. » Et Élisée dit : « Qu’il y ait pour moi, je te prie, une double part de ton esprit. »
fr.B: Quand ils eurent traversé, Élie dit à Élisée : « Avant que je sois enlevé loin de toi, dis-moi ce que je peux faire pour toi. » Élisée répondit : « Je t’en prie, que je reçoive une double part de ton esprit ! »
fr.R: Quand ils ont eu traversé, Élie a dit à Élisée : « Je vais bientôt être enlevé loin de toi. Avant que cela arrive, que puis-je faire pour toi ? Demande-le-moi. » Élisée a répondu : « S’il te plaît, donne-moi une double part de ton esprit, la part que reçoit le fils aîné. »

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokwisha kuvuka, Eliya akamwambia Elisha, "Omba nikufanyie nini kabla sijachukuliwa kutoka kwako." Elisha akasema, "Tafadhali, sehemu mara mbili ya roho yako na iwe kwangu."
sw.B: Walipokwisha kuvuka, Eliya alimwambia Elisha, "Kabla sijachukuliwa kutoka kwako, niambie nikufanyie nini." Elisha akajibu, "Tafadhali, nipate sehemu mara mbili ya roho yako."
sw.R: Walipokwisha kuvuka, Eliya akamwambia Elisha, "Ninakaribia kuchukuliwa nikuache. Kabla ya hayo, nikufanyie nini? Niombe." Elisha akajibu, "Tafadhali nipe sehemu mara mbili ya roho yako, ile sehemu anayopewa mwana mzaliwa wa kwanza."

vi.L: Khi họ đã đi qua, Ê-li nói với Ê-li-sê: "Hãy xin điều ta sẽ làm cho con trước khi ta bị cất khỏi con." Ê-li-sê nói: "Xin cho con được phần đôi thần linh của thầy."
vi.B: Khi đã qua sông, Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Trước khi ta bị cất khỏi con, con muốn ta làm gì cho con thì hãy xin." Ê-li-sê thưa: "Xin cho con được hưởng phần đôi thần linh của thầy."
vi.R: Khi đã qua sông, Ê-li bảo Ê-li-sê: "Ta sắp bị đem đi khỏi con rồi. Trước khi điều ấy xảy ra, con muốn ta làm gì cho con? Hãy xin đi." Ê-li-sê thưa: "Xin thầy cho con được phần đôi thần linh của thầy, là phần dành cho con trai trưởng."

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 건넜을 때에, 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "내가 너에게서 데려감을 받기 전에 내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주어야 할지 구하여라." 그러자 엘리사가 말했다. "선생님의 영의 두 몫이 제게 있게 해 주십시오."
ko.B: 그들이 건너간 뒤에 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "내가 너에게서 떠나기 전에 내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주면 좋을지 말해 보아라." 엘리사가 대답했다. "선생님의 영이 제게 갑절로 임하게 해 주십시오."
ko.R: 강을 건넌 뒤에 엘리야가 엘리사에게 말했다. "나는 곧 너를 떠나 하늘로 올라가게 된다. 그 전에 내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주면 좋겠느냐? 말해 보아라." 엘리사가 대답했다. "선생님의 영을 갑절로 받게 해 주십시오. 맏아들이 받는 몫처럼 말입니다."

decisions.choice: a mouth of two: a double portion, the share of the firstborn heir
alternatives: twice as much of your spirit as you have
decisions.reason: "A mouth of two" is the phrase the law uses for the firstborn son's inheritance: he receives a double share of what his father leaves (Deuteronomy 21:17). Elisha is not asking to be twice as great as Elijah. He asks to be Elijah's chief heir and successor, the son who carries on his father's work (verse 12). In Zechariah 13:8 the same phrase means two parts out of three, which also fits the idea of the larger share.

decisions.choice: your spirit: the power of God at work in Elijah as a prophet
decisions.reason: Elijah's spirit is the prophetic power with which Yahweh filled him. The prophets later see that this spirit now rests on Elisha (verse 15), as Yahweh once put the spirit that was on Moses on the elders (Numbers 11:17, 25).

decisions.choice: you: Elisha, in a less common spelling
decisions.reason: The word for "you" is written here and in verse 10 in a form that usually speaks to a woman. It is an older or local way of writing the word for a man, and it still means Elisha.

decisions.choice: the share that goes to a firstborn son
decisions.reason: Readable explains the double portion, as m1 does, so that the reader does not take it to mean twice Elijah's power.

decisions.choice: I am about to be taken away from you. Before that happens, what can I do for you?
decisions.reason: Readable splits Elijah's request into short sentences.

decisions.choice: una doble porción
decisions.reason: "Doble porción" keeps the picture of the firstborn's share of an inheritance (m1) and avoids "el doble", which would mean twice Elijah's power; Readable adds the explanation, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "une double part"
decisions.reason: The "mouth of two" is the double share of the firstborn heir (meaning decision); "une double part" says the share without suggesting twice Elijah’s power.

decisions.choice: "sehemu mara mbili"
decisions.reason: Swahili "sehemu mara mbili" (a double share) keeps the picture of the heir's portion rather than "twice your spirit"; Readable adds the firstborn son, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "phần đôi thần linh của thầy"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "mouth of two" is the double share of the firstborn heir (m1), not twice as much as Elijah had; "phần đôi" says a share. "Thần linh" in lowercase is the power of God at work in the prophet (m2), as the style guide uses "thần linh" where it is not a name.

decisions.choice: "두 몫" (L), "갑절로" (B, R) for "a mouth of two", with Readable naming the firstborn's share
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as the double share of the firstborn heir (Deuteronomy 21:17); Literal keeps "two portions", Balanced and Readable say "double".

decisions.choice: "하늘로 올라가게 된다" at Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "taken from you"; Readable makes the passive clear in Korean, which has no easy passive for "be taken", using what verse 1 has told the reader.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, You have made hard to ask; if you see me taken from with you, let it be to you so; and if not, it will not be.

en.L: And he said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it will not be [so]."
en.B: Elijah said, "You have asked for something difficult. If you see me being taken from you, you will have it; if you do not, you will not."

fr.B: Élie dit : « Tu demandes une chose difficile. Si tu me vois quand je serai enlevé loin de toi, cela te sera accordé ; sinon, cela ne te sera pas accordé. »

decisions.choice: you have made it hard to ask: what you ask is difficult

decisions.choice: if you see me taken: seeing is the sign that the request is granted
decisions.reason: To see Elijah taken up is to be allowed to see what is hidden from others, as Elisha's servant later sees the fiery horses and chariots around them (6:17). If Yahweh opens Elisha's eyes to it, he has also given him Elijah's spirit.

decisions.choice: Elijah said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: walking, walking and speaking: they went on talking as they walked
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows that they kept on walking and talking. The last thing the two do together is talk.

decisions.choice: chariot of fire and horses of fire: Yahweh's heavenly army
decisions.reason: Fire often shows Yahweh's presence (Exodus 3:2; 19:18). Chariots and horses were the strongest force of an army; these of fire belong to Yahweh's own host, as the horses and chariots of fire around Elisha do later (6:17).

decisions.choice: Elijah went up in the whirlwind: the chariot separates them, the wind takes him up
decisions.reason: The chariot and horses come between the two men; the text says that Elijah went up "in the whirlwind", as verse 1 said. It does not say that he rode in the chariot.

decisions.choice: Elijah went up to heaven: he did not die
decisions.reason: Elijah is taken alive, as Enoch was taken by God (Genesis 5:24). Unlike Moses, whose death and burial are told (Deuteronomy 34:5-6), Elijah has no grave. Malachi 3:23 later promises that he will be sent again before the day of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: [came] / came between
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the sight before the reader with "look" and then says that the horses separated the two; English needs a verb of coming.

decisions.choice: "cỗ xe lửa"
decisions.reason: "Xe lửa" alone is the modern word for a train; "cỗ xe lửa" with "những con ngựa lửa" keeps the chariot clear.

decisions.choice: "불 병거" for the chariot of fire at every level
decisions.reason: "병거" is the word the Samuel drafts and the terms note use for chariots; Readable keeps it here because it is linked to Elisha's cry in verse 12 and to 6:17.

decisions.choice: my father: a title of honor for the prophet who led him
decisions.reason: Elisha calls his master "father" as a disciple honors his teacher; the members of a company of prophets were called its "sons" (verse 3). The cry is also one of grief at a father's loss, and Elisha is the son who inherits (verse 9).

decisions.choice: the chariots of Israel and its horsemen: Elijah was Israel's true defense
alternatives: Elisha names the fiery chariot and horses he is watching
decisions.reason: Chariots and horsemen were a kingdom's strength in war. Elisha's cry most likely means that Elijah, through whom Yahweh worked, did more to protect Israel than all its chariots. King Joash says the same words over the dying Elisha (13:14). It is also possible that Elisha is naming the fiery chariot and horses he sees (verse 11) as Israel's real army, Yahweh's own.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes in two: mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the usual sign of grief at a death (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 1:11). Elisha mourns, and then takes up Elijah's cloak in place of his own torn garment (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is singular but means chariots as a force, as in 1 Kings 9:22.

decisions.choice: could not see Elijah
decisions.reason: Readable names Elijah where the Hebrew has "him".

decisions.choice: carros de Israel y su caballería (Literal); carros ... y jinetes (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The singular Hebrew word means chariots as a force, so Spanish says "carros"; Balanced and Readable say "jinetes", as the terms note's "carros y jinetes".

decisions.choice: "Toi, les chars et les cavaliers d’Israël !"
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Toi" so that the cry is heard as said of Elijah, Israel’s true defense (meaning decision), not as a sight of chariots.

decisions.choice: "magari ya vita ... na wapanda farasi"
decisions.reason: The terms note's "magari ya vita na wapanda farasi" for Israel's chariot force; the Hebrew singular stands for the chariots as a body, which Swahili gives with the plural.

decisions.choice: "Cha ơi"
decisions.reason: Elisha cries out the title of honor "my father" (m1); Vietnamese keeps "cha" in this cry, though he has called Elijah "thầy" until now.

decisions.choice: "Ngài là xe chiến mã ..."
decisions.reason: Readable says outright that the title is about Elijah, Israel's true defense (m2); "ngài" here is a respectful word for a man, without a capital span.

decisions.choice: The cry addresses Elijah with the honorific vocative "이시여" at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps the plain "이여"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the title as said of Elijah himself (Israel's true defense); the honorific shows Korean readers that it is Elijah who is addressed, not the army.
